Definition: from G4483; an utterance (individually, collectively or specially),; by implication, a matter or topic (especially of narration, command or dispute); with a negative naught whatever:--+ evil, + nothing, saying, word.
KeyPassages: Matthew 4:4; Luke 1:37; John 6:68; Romans 10:17; Ephesians 6:17; 1 Peter 1:25
BiblicalUsage: Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God, and with God nothing shall be impossible, for no word of His is without power. Peter confessed, Lord, to whom shall we go? Thou hast the words of eternal life. Faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God, the sword of the Spirit is the word of God, and the word of the Lord endureth for ever.
TheologicalSignificance: I am convinced that the word is not only what God says but what God does, because His word carries His power with it. A word from God feeds a man, opens a womb, raises faith in a hearer, and cuts like a sword in the hand of the Spirit. I hold that the words of eternal life are not many words but one Word, and Peter was right to stay where He spoke.
RelatedBooks: Matthew; Luke; John; Romans; Ephesians; 1 Peter
